name: adrop
title: Drop dimensions of an array object

origin.description: Drop degenerate dimensions of an array object. Offers less automaticity and more control than the base drop() function. adrop() is a S3 generic, with one method, adrop.default, supplied in the abind package.
origin.usage: adrop(x, drop = TRUE, named.vector = TRUE, one.d.array = FALSE, ...)

arguments.name: drop
arguments.text: A logical or numeric vector describing exactly which dimensions to drop. It is intended that this argument be supplied always. The default is very rarely useful (drop=TRUE means drop the first dimension of a 1-d array).

arguments.name: named.vector
arguments.text: Optional, defaults to TRUE. Controls whether a vector result has names derived from the dimnames of x.

arguments.name: one.d.array
arguments.text: Optional, defaults to FALSE. If TRUE, a one-dimensional array result will be an object with a dim attribute of length 1, and possibly a dimnames attribute. If FALSE, a one-dimensional result will be a vector object (named if named.vector==TRUE).
There are no additional arguments allowed for adrop.default but other methods may use them.

origin.details: Dimensions can only be dropped if their extent is one, i.e., dimension i of array x can be dropped only if dim(x)[i]==1. It is an error to request adrop to drop a dimension whose extent is not 1. A 1-d array can be converted to a named vector by supplying drop=NULL (which means drop no dimensions, and return a 1-d array result as a named vector).
origin.value: If x is an object with a dim attribute (e.g., a matrix or array), then adrop returns an object like x, but with the requested extents of length one removed. Any accompanying dimnames attribute is adjusted and returned with x.
origin.example:
x <- array(1:24,dim=c(2,3,4),dimnames=list(letters[1:2],LETTERS[1:3],letters[23:26]))
print(adrop(x[1,,,drop=FALSE],drop=1))
print(adrop(x[,1,,drop=FALSE],drop=2))
print(adrop(x[,,1,drop=FALSE],drop=3))
print(adrop(x[1,1,1,drop=FALSE],drop=1))
print(adrop(x[1,1,1,drop=FALSE],drop=2))
print(adrop(x[1,1,1,drop=FALSE],drop=3))
print(adrop(x[1,1,1,drop=FALSE],drop=1:2))
print(adrop(x[1,1,1,drop=FALSE],drop=1:2,one.d=TRUE))
print(adrop(x[1,1,1,drop=FALSE],drop=1:2,named=FALSE))
print(dim(adrop(x[1,1,1,drop=FALSE],drop=1:2,one.d=TRUE)))
print(dimnames(adrop(x[1,1,1,drop=FALSE],drop=1:2,one.d=TRUE)))
print(names(adrop(x[1,1,1,drop=FALSE],drop=1:2,one.d=TRUE)))
print(dim(adrop(x[1,1,1,drop=FALSE],drop=1:2)))
print(dimnames(adrop(x[1,1,1,drop=FALSE],drop=1:2)))
print(names(adrop(x[1,1,1,drop=FALSE],drop=1:2)))

translation.description: Drop degenerate dimensions of an array object with explicit control over which margins are removed. This follows adrop.default from abind.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: An abind Array or NumPy array with at least two dimensions (matrices and higher-rank arrays).

arguments.name: drop
arguments.text: Dimension numbers to remove, a logical mask with one entry per dimension, character names of dimensions, or None to drop no dimensions.

arguments.name: named_vector
arguments.text: When a single dimension remains, return an R-style named vector from the surviving dimnames if True.

arguments.name: one_d_array
arguments.text: When a single dimension remains, keep a one-dimensional array with dim and dimnames instead of a vector.

arguments.name: **kwargs
arguments.text: Not allowed for this method; extra keywords raise an error.

translation.details: Only margins of length one may be dropped. Logical drop masks must match rank. Character drop matches names on the R dim vector when present. Results preserve column-major layout and dimnames on abind Array inputs.
translation.value: An abind Array when x is an Array; otherwise a NumPy array. One-dimensional results may be vectors or arrays depending on named_vector and one_d_array.
translation.example:
import numpy as np
from abind.abind import Array
from abind.adrop import adrop
from abind.asub import asub

x = Array(
    np.arange(1, 25).reshape((2, 3, 4), order="F"),
    dimnames=[list("ab"), list("ABC"), list("wxyz")],
)
scalar = asub(asub(asub(x, 1, 1, drop=False), 1, 2, drop=False), 1, 3, drop=False)
print(adrop(asub(x, 1, 1, drop=False), drop=1))
print(adrop(asub(x, 1, 2, drop=False), drop=2))
print(adrop(asub(x, 1, 3, drop=False), drop=3))
print(adrop(scalar, drop=1))
print(adrop(scalar, drop=2))
print(adrop(scalar, drop=3))
print(adrop(scalar, drop=[1, 2]))
print(adrop(scalar, drop=[1, 2], one_d_array=True))
print(adrop(scalar, drop=[1, 2], named_vector=False))
